name: Hair volumizer

lead: A hair volumizer is a styling or cleansing product made to make hair look thicker and lifted at the roots. It is aimed at flat, fine or thinning hair, so a person can get a fuller-looking head of hair in minutes.

It works by cosmetic means: polymers, proteins and silicones deposit on the hair shaft and make each strand bulkier and stiffer, and powders add grip and texture. The change is temporary and does not alter follicles or hair growth.

paras: Users apply a mousse or root-lifting spray to damp hair and blow-dry, use a volumizing shampoo and conditioner, or dust a texture powder at the roots. Many combine them with blow-drying techniques that lift hair at the crown and with haircuts that suit fine hair.
Product build-up can leave hair feeling stiff or heavy and may need a clarifying wash, and alcohol-heavy sprays can dry hair. Some people react to fragrance or ingredients in styling products.

angle.text: It makes hair look fuller on the day it is applied, which is useful for fine hair or thinning areas such as the crown and part. The result is cosmetic and temporary.

lead: A hair volumizer is a cosmetic product category designed to temporarily increase the body, fullness and lift of hair, especially fine, limp or thinning hair. Formats include shampoos and conditioners, mousses and foams, root-lifting sprays and dry powders.[1]

People use them to look as though they have denser hair. Products coat the shaft to swell its apparent diameter, deposit lightweight particles that provide root lift and texture, or increase friction between strands so hair stands off the scalp. Common ingredients include proteins, film-forming polymers and silicones.[1]
Volumizers change appearance rather than hair biology. They do not promote follicle health or reduce hair loss; the effect lasts until the hair is washed.[1]

paras: Liquid-based volumizers include shampoos, conditioners, mousses, foams and sprays. Mousses use soft copolymers to give hold with body, while root-lifting sprays often use polymers such as polyvinylpyrrolidone to build temporary structure at the roots.[1]
Dry volumizers include texture and volumizing powders, which absorb oil and add grit so hair stands away from the scalp.[1]

Volumizing formulas alter fiber stiffness, curvature and inter-fiber friction, so hair appears thicker and holds lift. Silicones such as dimethicone deposit on the cuticle to reduce limpness without weighing hair down.[1]
Volume products are part of hair-styling routines for men and women with fine or receding hair, often next to blow-drying and cuts that add height at the front or crown.
No studies found specific to hair volumizing products in peer-reviewed human trials. The literature on volumizing dermal fillers concerns injectable products for the face and is a separate topic.
